- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.

# Conservative Party Manifesto 2015: Summary

## Economic Plan and Fiscal Policy

The Conservatives presented their long-term economic plan as the foundation for all policies, emphasising Britain's recovery from the 2008 recession. Key commitments included eliminating the deficit by 2017-18 through £30 billion in fiscal consolidation, then running a budget surplus from 2018-19 onwards. The party pledged no increases to VAT, Income Tax, or National Insurance, while raising the Personal Allowance to £12,500 and the 40p tax threshold to £50,000. They promised to tackle tax evasion and pursue £5 billion annually from aggressive avoidance.

## Jobs and Business

The manifesto aimed for full employment, targeting two million new jobs and three million apprenticeships. Policies included abolishing employers' National Insurance for under-21s, supporting small businesses through rate reviews, and cutting £10 billion in red tape. The "Northern Powerhouse" initiative promised £13 billion in transport investment to rebalance the economy regionally.

## Welfare Reform

The Conservatives pledged to cap household benefits at £23,000 (down from £26,000), freeze working-age benefits for two years, and continue Universal Credit rollout. Young people aged 18-21 would face stricter conditions, including replacing Jobseeker's Allowance with time-limited Youth Allowance.

## Health and Education

NHS spending would increase by £8 billion above inflation by 2020, delivering seven-day GP access and same-day appointments for over-75s. Education commitments included 500 new free schools, converting failing schools to academies, and maintaining per-pupil funding.

## Immigration and Europe

The party maintained its aim of reducing net migration to tens of thousands, proposing EU welfare restrictions requiring four years' residency before accessing benefits. Crucially, they committed to an in-out EU referendum by end of 2017, seeking to renegotiate Britain's membership terms.

## Housing

Housing policies included 200,000 Starter Homes at 20% discount for first-time buyers under 40, extending Right to Buy to Housing Association tenants, and continuing Help to Buy schemes with a new Help to Buy ISA offering 25% government top-ups on deposits.

## Defence and Security

The Conservatives promised to maintain Trident nuclear deterrent, meet NATO's 2% GDP defence spending target, and invest £160 billion in military equipment over ten years. Counter-terrorism measures included new communications data legislation and Extremism Disruption Orders.

## Constitutional Reform

The manifesto pledged English votes for English laws, implementation of the Smith Commission for Scottish devolution, and scrapping the Human Rights Act in favour of a British Bill of Rights.

## Pensions and Retirement

The triple lock on state pensions would continue (rising by earnings, inflation, or 2.5%, whichever highest). Inheritance Tax changes would raise the effective threshold to £1 million for married couples through a new main residence allowance.
